thread:
alice_support: Customer (carla@acme-corp) opened an escalation: invoice shows ~3.2M billed tokens for Feb but dashboard 'served' tokens are ~1.9M. They say they only call our /generate once per request but have a post-processing reranker we run server-side. invoice id INV-2026-02-ACME attached. :frowning:

carla_cust: attaching a snippet of the request flow we do: we call Redwood to generate 2 candidates, then we call a separate reranker endpoint that consumes both candidates + our features and calls back into Redwood. We only thought the rerank was internal (no extra tokens) — where are the extra tokens coming from?

alice_support: Thanks Carla, filing here and triaging. Initial hypothesis: the reranker -> Redwood call is being metered as a separate request (input tokens + model output) which would explain extra billed tokens. Also need to check continuous-batcher + prefix/KV cache warmup behavior: if the reranker triggers separate small requests that don't hit the cache, they could be charged fully.

tim_eng: tagging the infra folks. Quick ask: can you paste one full request id or audit_id from the reranker call? we'll look up logs. Also did you enable postprocessing_batch_aggregation on your project? that changes internal routing.

carla_cust: audit_id=acme-2026-02-11-zz998. We have postprocessing_batch_aggregation enabled (default). We thought that would reduce charges because it aggregates calls.

jonathan_sre: grabbing logs for audit_id acme-2026-02-11-zz998. Raw trace shows 3 distinct upstream requests to our inference cluster: (1) original /generate for candidate set, (2) reranker /generate that includes original candidates as input, (3) a short metadata probe for postprocess routing. Billing meter events show tokens counted for all three. Looks like the reranker is a real model call and is billed.

alice_support: Is there any chance the reranker call benefits from KV/prefix cache hits (i.e., served < billed)? Or vice versa where warmup path causes billed > served?

jonathan_sre: Good question. For this trace: the reranker calls had low sequence lengths but were issued while our continuous-batcher was cold for that shard, so they were not aggregated into larger batches. Also KV-cache prefix hit rate was ~10% on reranker inputs. So billed tokens ~= raw tokens. The larger discrepancy seems to come from an additional internal 'postprocess-annotation' step that duplicates inputs for safety — two internal requests: one sanitized input and one for scoring. Both appear in billing pipeline.

mike_billing: FYI we recently changed metering to count "ingress tokens" at the API gateway level and "model output" as separate events. Historically some internal intermediate calls were collapsed into a single billing entry; that collapse logic skips when calls are made from different auth principals. If the reranker call uses a different API key or service account, it won't be collapsed and you'll see both billed.

carla_cust: Hmm the reranker originates from their server using the same customer API key. We verified they reuse the same key. Could the collapse logic still separate them?

tim_eng: Possible: postprocess aggregation spawns internal sub-requests that use a system principal (not the customer's API key) to route to scoring models. Those system-originated requests are not eligible for the "collapse same-customer requests" optimization. That would explain two billed entries per logical operation.

alice_support: OK — two parallel causes: (A) reranker is an actual additional model call, (B) internal postprocess safety probes are separate auth and prevent billing collapse. Either would increase billed tokens vs dashboard served tokens. We should confirm which is dominant for ACME.

jonathan_sre: Data we pulled: for INV-2026-02 ACME overall, there are ~620k tokens coming from requests marked as "system-principal" on their project during February. Those align with the times ACME's reranker runs. That suggests the postprocess safety duplication is a big chunk.

mike_billing: Action item for billing: run a query to recompute collapsed-billing view for ACME with a heuristic that treats system-principal subcalls with matching trace ids as collapsible. If agreeable, we can issue an invoice adj for the duplicated tokens.

alice_support: Agreed — before we propose adj, we should collect repro steps and a minimal curl that reproduces the double-billing so infra can reproduce and fix. Carla, can you run this minimal flow and post the trace IDs?

carla_cust: Sure. Minimal repro (we'll run shortly):

```bash
# 1) generate candidates
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"xsmall-rerank","input":"short prompt"}'
# note response ids
# 2) post candidates to reranker endpoint which (in our stack) triggers internal scoring calls
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"candidates":[...]}'
```

alice_support: thanks. Once you paste the response trace ids we'll cross-check with billing events. Meanwhile I'll open a follow-up ticket for infra to review collapse logic. @mike_billing can you prioritize the collapsed-view recompute for ACME?

mike_billing: On it. I'll run the recompute scoped to invoice INV-2026-02 and provide a diff. ETA EOD PST. :thumbsup:

jonathan_sre: Infra notes for fix: possible mitigations — (1) ensure system-principal subcalls inherit customer principal for billing hooks when trace id is same, (2) emit a metadata flag from postprocess indicating "internal_duplicate=true" so billing can skip, (3) tweak continuous-batcher warmup to reduce separate small calls when aggregation mode is enabled. I'll draft a short proposal.

alice_support: Great. Carla — want me to pause next invoice generation while billing reviews? Or do you want an immediate credit if recompute shows big delta?

carla_cust: We'll wait for recompute diff first. If it's >10% we'll request credit. Thanks for fast triage.

mike_billing: recompute started. Will drop a note with delta and a provisional credit if applicable.

observability-bot: [Alert] trace acme-2026-02-11-zz998 shows 3 model calls, KV cache hit rate 12%, continuous-batcher merge_count=0 (cold path).

alice_support: closing loop: once recompute is done we'll update ACME and add docs to support KB about rerankers and billing (short note: separate model calls + system principal duplicates can increase billed tokens).
